newsitem.title: USA: Equity Oil eyes possible $9 mln write-off.
newsitem.headline: Equity Oil eyes possible $9 mln write-off.

text.p: Equity Oil Co said on Monday its exploration project in Russia, Symskaya Exploration Inc, is continuing to evaluate the testing results from the Lemok No. 1 well in Eastern Siberia.
The company said that the project is also actively pursuing financing possibilities to fund the drilling of a second well at the project.

If Symskaya elects to abandon the Siberian project in its entirety, the company would be required to write off its equity investment in Symskaya of about $9.0 million as of September 30, a statement from Equity said.

The costs of the Lemok No. 1 well, about $5.0 million net to equity, will be capitalized as a component of total prospect costs. Further evaluation, including future drilling plans, of the prospect continues.
The company said the current environment of strong commodity prices, coupled with marked increases in production, helped the company post significant increases in revenues, cash flows and net income.

The company said that acquisition and exploration efforts have enabled it to replace more than 100 percent of forecast 1996 oil production. It said it is also makiing excellent progress towards replacing gas production.
Of the 16 wells it has participated in so far this year, eight have been completed as gas wells, three as oil wells, four are in progress and one has been abandoned.
At its 3D seismic project in the Sacramento Basin, the company said it has successfully drilled 11 out of 13 wells.
In addition, the company said it has 12 more wells planned for the balance of the year, including 10 in the Sacramento Basin.
